transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Um... my job sent me, mostly. I guess I've been having some issues keeping track of things. Just... forgetting scheduled callbacks, or work orders. Basic follow-ups I promised people. 

It's kind of piled up a lot lately, and... well, work basically told me I needed to come here before I lose my shot at moving up. So, here I am.
When did you first notice these problems with forgetting things and keeping track of work? Did it start suddenly, or has it been gradually getting worse over time?

Um... I guess it's been noticeably worse for about 11 months. 

That's when the new management company took over. They switched our department over to digital work orders and... well, stricter documentation. So... yeah. It just got harder to keep track of after that.
Around the time this started 11 months ago, did you have any major illness, injury, surgery, or start taking any new medications or substances?
Um... no. Nothing like that. I haven't been sick or had any surgeries. And I don't really take any medication, so... no.
Besides the trouble keeping track of things at work, have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed over these past 11 months?
Um... no. Not really. I haven't felt like that. Just... normal, I guess. I'm not depressed.
Before these 11 months ago when work changed, did you have any trouble with organization, attention, or remembering things in school, previous jobs, or in your personal life?

Um... yeah, I guess so. It's not just the new work stuff. 

I mean... even way back in grade school, I was kind of like this. My teachers used to say I was bright, but... I was always losing my papers. Or I'd miss parts of the directions they gave us. They always had to remind me to actually finish my work. So... yeah. It's always been there.
When you're trying to focus on a task or sit still, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, feeling restless, or having trouble staying in one place?
No, I don't really do that. I can sit still just fine. I just... my mind wanders, I guess, but I'm not restless or anything.
Do you find yourself acting or speaking without thinking things through first, or do people tell you that you interrupt them or jump into things too quickly?
No, not really. I don't think I do that. People don't complain about it, anyway.
When you were a child or teenager, did teachers or parents ever say you were hyperactive, had too much energy, or couldn't sit still in class or at home?
No... I don't remember anyone ever saying that. I wasn't really a hyper kid. Just quiet, mostly.

When you're working on a project or task, do you have trouble getting started, organizing your approach, or breaking it down into steps — or is it more that you start okay but just forget details or lose focus partway through?
I don't know. I guess... I just have trouble with all of it. Getting started is hard. Staying with it is hard. It just doesn't get done.

When you were in school, did you ever have particular trouble with reading, spelling, writing, or math compared to other subjects — or was it more of a general difficulty staying organized and paying attention across everything?
I don't think it was a specific subject. I didn't have trouble reading or anything like that. It was just... hard to pay attention to any of it, really.

Outside of work, in your personal life or relationships, have these attention and organizational problems caused you trouble — like with managing your home, paying bills, keeping appointments, or things like that?

I don't really know about home. It's... mostly work that's the problem, honestly. It's turned into a pretty serious issue there. I've got this big backlog of work orders... tenants are complaining. I even have a safety review on my record now. I've been working toward a promotion for a while, and... I'm just scared this is going to cost me that.

When you're at home on your own time — managing bills, organizing your space, keeping track of personal appointments or commitments to friends — do you run into similar problems with forgetting things or staying organized, or is it really just been a work issue?
I don't really know. Like I said, it's mostly work. I just... I don't really notice those kinds of problems at home. It's just work where it's all piling up.

When you think back to your childhood or teenage years — not just school, but at home too — did your parents or family ever complain that you were disorganized, forgetful, or had trouble keeping your room clean, doing chores, or remembering to do things they asked you to do?

I mean... yeah, I guess I've been this way since grade school. Long before any of this pressure at my job. I don't remember much about chores, but... teachers used to tell my parents I was bright. I just... I always misplaced my papers. Or I'd miss parts of the directions they gave us. They always had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So... yeah. I guess it's been a while.
